title: New web VM unreachable although a firewall rule 'allows it'
intro: web-3 was just created in europe-west1-d from a copied command. It has an external IP, nginx is running, and the firewall rule allow-https-web opens 443 to the world. Yet https://35.205.9.40 times out, while web-1 and web-2 work.

steps.prompt: Show the network tags of web-3 (europe-west1-d).
expected_commands: gcloud compute instances describe web-3 --zone europe-west1-d --format="value(tags.items)"
gcloud compute instances describe web-3 --zone europe-west1-d
steps.hint: Firewall rules select VMs by network tag.

steps.prompt: Show which tags the rule allow-https-web targets.
The rule targets 'web'; web-3 only has the console's default http-server/https-server tags (which only match the default network's rules). Compare with web-1 in europe-west1-b.
expected_commands: gcloud compute instances describe web-1 --zone europe-west1-b --format="value(tags.items)"
gcloud compute instances describe web-1 --zone europe-west1-b
gcloud compute instances add-tags web-3 --zone europe-west1-d --tags web

steps.prompt: Verify from outside: request https://35.205.9.40 with a 5-second limit, printing only the HTTP status code.

resolution: GCP firewall rules don't attach to VMs; they select VMs by network tag (or service account). web-3 was created with the console's 'Allow HTTPS traffic' checkbox, which adds the https-server tag. That tag only matches the default-allow-https rule on the auto-created 'default' network, not the custom rule on prod-vpc, which targets 'web'. So nothing allowed 443 to this VM, and the implied deny-all ingress dropped it: a timeout, not a refusal. Comparing a working VM with the broken one found the difference in two commands. Prevention: create VMs from an instance template or Terraform module, where tags are defined once, never from a copied console command; and for security-relevant rules, consider targeting service accounts, which are harder to set by accident.
